explain: equivalent 是相等的，符合兩種測試同樣準確；因此可選較便宜者，用 Therefore（因此），不是 In contrast（相較之下）。

subject: english
q: The two accounts ____ each other: one says noon, the other midnight. ____, we cannot accept both.
explain: 兩種時間不同，表示證詞 contradict（互相矛盾），不是 confirm（證實）；不能都採信是結果，用 Consequently。

subject: english
q: Participation is ____. ____, students must attend rather than choose whether to join.
explain: 必須出席表示 compulsory（強制的）；後句改述前句意義，用 In other words（換句話說）。

subject: english
q: While ____ for her turn, Lea read a novel ____ her brother had lent her.
explain: Lea 主動等待，用 waiting；novel 是先行詞，關係子句缺 lent 的受詞，用 which，不用 what。

subject: english
q: ____ the safety course, Jo could explain ____ the alarm worked.
explain: Jo 主動完成課程，可用 Having completed 或 After having completed；被動式不符主詞。警報如何運作應用 how「如何」，不用 what。

subject: english
q: The tools ____ in this box belong to the artist ____ studio we built.
explain: 工具被存放，用 stored 縮減被動關係子句；whose studio 表藝術家的工作室，關係詞須表所有關係。

subject: english
q: Although ____ a place on the team, Hana chose a job ____ allowed her to work outdoors.
explain: Hana 是被提供名額，用 offered 縮減讓步子句；job 有先行詞，後接 that 作關係子句主詞。

subject: english
q: ____ the system been tested, the error ____ detected before yesterday's launch.
explain: 與過去事實相反，用 Had 引導倒裝條件句；錯誤本來會被發現，用 would have been detected。

subject: english
q: Our security system has always been weak; if it were stronger, the files ____ ____ last night.
explain: 系統一向薄弱，假設較強的持續狀態可影響昨晚結果；過去未實現的被動結果用 would not have been stolen（本不會被偷）。

subject: english
q: ____ I free today, I would join you, but my boss ____ me three urgent tasks since breakfast.
explain: 與現在事實相反的倒裝條件句用 Were I free；since breakfast 連到現在，主句用 has given。

subject: english
q: I wish the brakes ____ checked before yesterday's ride; the accident ____ while we were going down a hill.
explain: wish 對過去未檢查表示遺憾，用 had been checked；昨天發生事故用 occurred，不用現在完成式。

subject: english
q: Seats were ____, so not until another chair arrived ____ everyone sit down.
explain: limited 是有限的，符合須再搬椅子；not until 置句首使主句倒裝，過去能力用 could。

subject: english
q: The ____ mistakes you make, the less time you ____ correcting them.
explain: mistakes 是可數複數，用 fewer；錯誤越少，浪費於訂正的時間越少，用 waste。

subject: english
q: Please explain ____ for everyone to understand; your current explanation is too ____.
explain: explain 用副詞 simply（簡單地）修飾，enough 放副詞後；目前說明太 complex（複雜的），所以需要簡化。

subject: english
q: I would rather you ____ the invitation yesterday; your refusal made the host feel ____.
explain: 對他人過去行為的偏好用 would rather 加過去完成式 had accepted；遭拒後感到 hurt（難過），不是 grateful（感激的）。

subject: english
q: To ____ her identity, the witness insisted on ____ behind a screen during the interview.
explain: 屏風用來隱藏身分，故用 conceal；on 後接動名詞，being seated 表示坐著或就座。seat 表示使人入座時須接受詞，不能用 seating 表示自己坐下。

subject: english
q: The athlete seems ____ ____ from the tournament last week; her name is missing from the final list.
explain: 退出發生在上週且早於現在的推測，用 to have withdrawn；withdraw from 是退出，recruit 是招募。

subject: english
q: The group raised money ____ its reading program, hoping ____ free lessons next year.
explain: sustain 是維持，符合募款延續計畫；hope 後接不定詞 to offer（提供）。

subject: english
q: Ben was ____ to apply because he feared ____ by the interviewers.
explain: reluctant 是不情願的，符合害怕面試結果；Ben 是被拒絕，用被動動名詞 being rejected。

subject: english
q: Rather than keep the broken bike, we ____ ____ a new one and now ride it daily.
explain: 後文已買車且每天騎，應用 agreed（同意），不是 refused（拒絕）；agree 後接不定詞 to buy（購買）。

subject: english
q: ____ too much on decorations left us without enough money to ____ the band.
explain: Spending（花費）作主詞，不能用過去式 Spent；須花錢聘請樂團用 hire，fire 是解僱。

subject: english
q: After the race, we stopped ____ and drank water to ____ our strength.
explain: stopped to rest 是停下原活動去休息；喝水是為了 recover（恢復）體力，不是 reduce（減少）。

subject: english
q: I immediately knew who she was: I ____ her voice when I heard her ____.
explain: 立刻知道是誰表示 recognized（認出）聲音，不是 forgot（忘記）；heard 後接受詞與原形 sing（唱歌），不能接 sang。

subject: english
q: We are satisfied ____ ____ the team has achieved despite its tiny budget.
explain: be satisfied with 是對……滿意；what 兼作 achieved 的受詞，that 不能補出缺少的受詞。

subject: english
q: You qualify ____ a refund ____ you return the unused ticket before Friday.
explain: qualify for 加名詞表示符合資格；provided that（只要）後接條件子句，despite 不能直接接完整子句。

subject: english
q: Pay attention ____ the label, ____ tells you how to store the medicine.
explain: pay attention to 是注意；which 引導非限定關係子句，指前面的 label，不能用 what。

subject: english
q: ____ they were innocent, the prisoners were deprived ____ their freedom.
explain: Although 後接完整讓步子句；be deprived of 是被剝奪，這裡指自由被剝奪。

subject: english
q: There was strong ____ to the fee; most members disliked it. ____, the council rejected it.
explain: 形容詞 strong 後接名詞 opposition（反對）；議會否決收費提案是反對所造成的結果，用 Consequently（因此）。

subject: english
q: The road crossing was ____. ____, we used the bridge to reach the other side safely.
explain: was 後用形容詞 unsafe（不安全的）；改走人行橋是替代方案，用 Instead（改為），非 Similarly（同樣地）。

subject: english
q: The team worked ____. ____, it finished later than the slower group because its task was much larger.
explain: 修飾 worked 用副詞 efficiently（有效率地）；有效率卻較晚完成，用 Nevertheless 表轉折。

subject: english
q: The room needs ____. ____, the broken windows must be replaced.
explain: needs 後需名詞 improvement（改善）；換掉破窗是改善的例子，用 For example，並非反駁前句。

subject: english
q: Her ____ ____ she would repay the loan reassured us.
explain: Her 後需名詞 assurance（保證）；that 引導同位語子句說明保證內容，後面子句不缺成分。

subject: english
q: We need a ____ assistant ____ can check the records without making errors.
explain: 修飾 assistant 用形容詞 reliable（可靠的）；關係代名詞在子句中作主詞，用 who，不用 whom。

subject: english
q: ____ the ropes looked strong, we decided to ____ them before the climb.
explain: Although 後接完整子句；to 後接原形動詞 strengthen（加強），不能用名詞 strength。

subject: english
q: The machine runs ____ ____ its simple design, which has fewer moving parts.
explain: 修飾 runs 用副詞 efficiently（有效率地）；its simple design 是名詞片語，原因用 because of。

subject: english
q: So ____ was the noise that ____ hear the speaker.
explain: was 後接形容詞 loud（大聲的）；so...that 的倒裝在主句，that 子句仍用正常語序 we could barely。

subject: english
q: Never before ____ such ____ from a waiter; his insults shocked us.
explain: Never before 置句首需倒裝 have we；such 後此處需名詞 rudeness（無禮），不是形容詞 rude。

subject: english
q: The more ____ the directions are, the ____ mistakes beginners make.
explain: are 前的補語要用形容詞 precise（精確的）；mistakes 是可數複數，連動比較用 fewer。

subject: english
q: It was because of her ____ that ____ her account.
explain: because of 後需名詞 honesty（誠實）；強調句 that 後維持正常語序 we believed，不倒裝。

subject: english
q: The files that ____ damaged since the pipe burst are the ones ____ we must copy first.
explain: files 是複數，since 連到現在，用 have been damaged；ones 有先行詞，後面的受詞關係代名詞用 which。

subject: english
q: Keep your receipt ____ the refund ____ next week; you may need it as proof of purchase.
explain: until 後接完整時間子句，during 不行；未來時間副詞子句用現在式，退款被支付，用 is paid。

subject: english
q: The guard asked ____ when the alarm ____ last night.
choices: what was I doing / has gone off
what I was doing / has gone off
what I was doing / went off
what was I doing / went off
explain: 間接問句用直述語序 what I was doing；last night 明示過去時間，警報響起用 went off，不用 has gone off。

subject: english
q: ____ the documents ____ before the fire or not remained unknown.
explain: 主詞位置的是否子句用 Whether，不用 If；文件在火災前被複製，用過去完成式被動 had been copied。

subject: english
q: When we visited last June, the house ____. ____, it had stood empty for years.
explain: 修復早於六月探訪，用 had been restored（已被修復）；修復前的空置狀態用 Previously（先前），不是表同樣地的 Likewise。

subject: english
q: The service ____ twice since Monday. ____, customers still praise its speed.
explain: since Monday 連到現在，用 has failed；故障卻仍受稱讚，用 Nevertheless（儘管如此）表轉折。

subject: english
q: In 2020, engineers said the dam ____ the following year. ____, the dam was finished in 2025.
explain: 從2020年轉述未來且水壩被完工，用 would be finished；In fact（事實上）補述實際2025年才完工，Likewise 表同樣地。

subject: english
q: By tomorrow's opening, all seats ____. ____, buying a seat at the door will be impossible.
explain: 到明天開場前座位將已售出，用 will have been sold，been 後接過去分詞 sold；無法現場買票是結果，用 Consequently（因此）。

subject: english
q: ____ Ana stopped ____ late at night, she would sleep better now.
explain: Had Ana stopped 等於 If Ana had stopped，假設過去已停止；停止吃用 stop eating，不能接 eaten。

subject: english
q: Only after the doors opened ____ heard ____ the first note.
explain: Only after 置句首，主句需倒裝 was the singer；感官動詞改被動後，用 heard to sing。

subject: english
q: The listeners yawned from lack of interest. The more ____ they felt, the ____ the speaker planned to end the talk.
explain: 打呵欠且失去興趣，表示聽眾感到 bored（無聊的），不是 boring（令人無聊的）；連動比較用 sooner（越早），不用最高級 soonest。

subject: english
q: It was on Tuesday that ____ the damaged screen ____ by a technician.
explain: 強調句 that 後維持 we had 的正常語序；have 加受詞加 replaced 表請人更換，螢幕是被更換的。

subject: english
q: With wells empty, a ____ of clean water left the village ____ to disease.
explain: lack 是缺乏，符合水井乾涸；缺水使村民 vulnerable to disease（易受疾病侵害），不是 immune（有免疫力的）。

subject: english
q: The spill caused serious ____, so the town hired experts to ____ the river.
explain: spill 造成 damage（損害）；聘請專家是為了 restore（恢復）河川狀況，不是 contaminate（污染）。

subject: english
q: The report contains a ____ the author admits inventing; we must stay ____ about its accuracy.
explain: 作者承認捏造的是 lie（謊言），不是 fact（事實）；因此須 skeptical（懷疑的），不能對準確性有信心。

subject: english
q: We need another ____: the original plan is not ____ with our limited funds.
explain: 原方案經費不足，所以需要另一個 choice（選擇）；原計畫不 feasible（可行的），compulsory 是強制的。

subject: english
q: We must comply ____ the rules; refusing could ____ our jobs and get us fired.
explain: comply with 是遵守；可能被解僱表示拒絕會 endanger（危及）工作，而非 secure（確保）工作。

subject: english
q: We have run ____ cooking oil, so our supplies are ____ and we cannot prepare dinner.
explain: run out of 是用完；因此 supplies are exhausted（物資耗盡），不會是 abundant（充足的）。

subject: english
q: The neighbors decided to ____ through a ____: music could play by day but must stop at nine.
explain: make up 此處指和好，fall out 指鬧翻；白天可放音樂、晚上須停止，兼顧雙方需求，是 compromise（妥協）。

subject: english
q: We must take the safety risk into ____ because protecting lives is our main ____.
explain: take...into account 是將……納入考量；保護生命是 priority（優先事項），obstacle 是障礙。

subject: english
q: To ____ the shelter, Mia signed ____ for a weekend of unpaid work. 'support / up' fits both blanks.
explain: support 是支持，符合投入無薪工作；sign up for 是報名參加，因此兩格都正確。

subject: english
q: ____ he was tired, Ben ____ to help; he said yes without hesitation. 'Although / refused' fits both blanks.
explain: Although（雖然）可接完整子句；Ben 毫不猶豫答應幫忙，應填 agreed（同意），不是 refused（拒絕）。

subject: english
q: We expected safe stairs, but they were ____. ____, we avoided them. 'dangerous / Nevertheless' fits both blanks.
explain: dangerous（危險的）符合避開樓梯的原因；後句是結果，應用 Therefore（因此），不能用表轉折的 Nevertheless（儘管如此）。

subject: english
q: The residents had to ____ ____ the river had flooded their homes. 'evacuate / because' fits both blanks.
explain: evacuate 是撤離，符合住家淹水的情境；because 後接完整子句，說明撤離原因。

subject: english
q: The chair demanded that each member ____ the ____ before the meeting. 'read / agenda' fits both blanks.
explain: demand 表要求時，that 子句用原形 read；agenda 是議程，符合會議前閱讀的情境。

subject: english
q: Please ____ an effort to explain the difference ____. 'make / clear' fits both blanks.
explain: make an effort 是努力；修飾 explain（解釋）須用副詞 clearly（清楚地），不能用形容詞 clear。

subject: english
q: Lena used ____ jog every morning, ____ she? 'to / didn't' fits both blanks.
explain: used to V 表過去習慣；肯定敘述的附加問句用否定式 didn't she，兩格都正確。

subject: english
q: The show was ____, not canceled. ____, it took place later. 'called off / In fact' fits both blanks.
explain: called off 是取消，與 not canceled 矛盾，應改 put off（延期）；In fact 補充稍後仍演出的事實。

subject: english
q: The ____ of the package ____ confirmed yesterday. 'arrival / has been' fits both blanks.
explain: arrival（抵達）是名詞，可接 of the package；yesterday 明示過去時間，被動應用 was confirmed（已獲確認），不是 has been confirmed。

subject: english
q: The proposal seemed ____, so we agreed ____ it a try. 'promising / to give' fits both blanks.
explain: promising 是有前景的，作 seemed 的補語；agree 後接不定詞 to give，兩格都正確。

subject: english
q: Seldom ____ the museum ____ closed for so long. 'has / being' fits both blanks.
explain: Seldom「很少」置句首引發倒裝，兩格依序填 has、been；has 後用 be 的過去分詞 been，不用現在分詞 being。

subject: english
q: Only after Jo explained ____ we understand ____ the alarm worked. 'did / how' fits both blanks.
explain: Only after 置句首，主句倒裝成 did we understand；how 引導名詞子句，表示警報如何運作，兩格都正確。

subject: english
q: We chose ____ more plastic. ____, we refilled our old bottles. 'not to buy / Instead' fits both blanks.
explain: chose not to buy 是選擇不買；改用舊瓶是替代方案，用 Instead（改為），兩格都正確。

subject: english
q: I didn't save it; if I had, I ____ it now. ____, I need to rewrite it. 'will have / Therefore' fits both blanks.
explain: 應填 would have、Therefore；would have it now 是「現在就會有它」，have 是主要動詞，不是完成式助動詞；未存檔，因此得重寫。

subject: english
q: The leak caused most losses; it was the ____ cause. We checked it ____. 'principal / thoroughly' fits both blanks.
explain: 造成大部分損失，故為 principal（主要的）原因；修飾 checked 用 thoroughly（徹底地），兩格都正確。

subject: english
q: The files ____ ____ online right now so everyone can read them. 'are being / concealed' fits both blanks.
explain: right now 配合 are being 表正在被處理；供大家閱讀表示 disclosed（公開），不是 concealed（隱藏）。

subject: english
q: We apologized ____ keeping the guests ____ outside. 'for / waited' fits both blanks.
explain: apologize for 是為……道歉；keep the guests waiting 表讓客人持續等候，用主動的 waiting（等待），不能用 waited。

subject: english
q: ____ we left, Jo was already asleep. ____, she missed our goodbye. 'By the time / Consequently' fits both blanks.
explain: By the time 加子句表示到某時；Jo 已睡著而錯過道別是因果關係，用 Consequently（因此）。

subject: english
q: The volunteers pledged ____ the forest by avoiding ____ trees. 'to conserve / cut down' fits both blanks.
explain: conserve 是保育，pledge 後接 to conserve 正確；avoid 後需動名詞，應改 cutting down（砍伐）。

subject: english
q: Not until the speech ended ____ we understand its ____. 'did / significance' fits both blanks.
explain: Not until 置句首需主句倒裝 did we understand；its 後接名詞 significance（意義），兩格都正確。

subject: english
q: The student ____ won yesterday's match ____ the trophy home last night. 'who / took' fits both blanks.
explain: who 在關係子句作主詞，指 student；last night 是明確過去時間，主句用 took（帶走）。

subject: english
q: The ice makes the road ____, so we recommend ____ until it melts. 'slippery / to wait' fits both blanks.
explain: slippery（濕滑的）符合結冰路面；recommend 後直接接動名詞，應為 waiting（等待），不能用 to wait。

subject: english
q: A: Could we meet at six? B: ____ A: I mean six in the evening.
choices: Would you like me to book a table?
Do you mean morning or evening?
Could we choose a different day?
How long do you plan to stay?
explain: I mean 是「我的意思是」；後句補充晚上六點，因此應先問 morning or evening「上午或晚上」，釐清時間。

subject: english
q: What do red envelopes represent at Lunar New Year in Taiwan?
choices: Thanks for help with preparing dinner.
Rewards for success in school exams.
Wishes for good luck in the year ahead.
Money earned for work done for the family.
explain: 農曆新年的紅包傳達對收禮者的祝福，象徵平安與好運；good luck 是「好運」。

subject: english
q: In Japan, which use of chopsticks at a meal is associated with funerals?
choices: Laying them on a rest beside the bowl.
Using them to lift food from your own plate.
Tapping them on the edge of a rice bowl.
Standing them upright in a bowl of rice.
explain: 在日本，將筷子直插飯中會使人聯想到祭祀亡者，是用餐禁忌；upright 是「直立地」，funeral 是「喪禮」。

subject: english
q: At dinner, a guest sees eye contact as rude; the host sees it as polite. Why might they misunderstand each other?
choices: They give the same behavior different meanings.
They have different levels of skill in English.
They have different interests in the meal's topic.
They have different amounts of time for the meal.
explain: eye contact 是「眼神接觸」；同一行為在雙方的文化觀點中代表不同意義，可能因此把對方的禮貌誤讀為失禮。

subject: english
q: A guide describes a country's dining customs. What best reveals a visitor's own food preferences?
choices: Ask the visitor which foods they enjoy eating.
Follow the guide's account of typical local meals.
Ask someone else who has the same nationality.
Use the rules for formal dinners in that country.
explain: preferences 是「偏好」；要了解個人喜歡哪些食物，應直接詢問本人，不能以同國籍者的習慣或文化介紹代替。

subject: english
q: Canada celebrates a harvest holiday in October; the United States, in November. These holidays fall in the same month.
explain: harvest holiday 是「慶祝收穫的節日」；加拿大感恩節在十月，美國在十一月，月份不同，題幹末句與前文不符。

subject: english
q: A festival keeps its old songs but adds new dances. It shows both cultural change and continuity.
explain: continuity 是「延續」；保留舊歌是文化傳承，加入新舞是文化變遷，兩者能並存。

subject: english
q: Use running water to ____ the soap off the cup without rubbing or soaking it.
explain: 流動清水洗去肥皂，且排除搓擦與浸泡，應選rinse＝沖洗；soak＝浸泡，wipe＝擦拭，polish＝磨亮。

subject: english
q: To mail the scarf flat, ____ it once along the middle.
explain: flat與along the middle提示沿中線對折；fold＝摺疊，roll＝捲起，twist＝扭轉。

subject: english
q: The lid was too ____; water escaped around its edge.
explain: 水從蓋子邊緣流出，表示沒有鎖緊；loose＝鬆的，tight＝緊的，stiff＝僵硬的。

subject: english
q: The river is ____ here; I can stand with the water below my knees.
explain: 水位低於膝蓋是在說深度；shallow＝淺的，narrow＝狹窄的，smooth＝平滑的。

subject: english
q: Their friendship grew warmer after a joke ended months of silence. 'Warmer' means ____.
explain: 笑話打破長期沉默，使友誼更親近；warmer在此＝更融洽的，不是更公開、正式或歷史更久。

subject: english
q: The printer swallowed my last sheet and stopped. 'Swallowed' means ____.
explain: 印表機把紙吞進去後停住；swallow＝吞嚥，此處轉指捲入，未說印兩次或切半。

subject: english
q: The news hit Rosa hard; she cried all evening. Here, 'hit' describes an emotional effect.
explain: 哭了一晚顯示消息造成情緒衝擊；hit hard＝造成沉重打擊，並非身體被打。

subject: english
q: The club has deep roots in town: three generations have joined. 'Roots' refers to its future plans.
explain: 三代居民參與指向過去建立的深厚連結；roots＝根基，不是未來計畫。

subject: english
q: The choir weathered a year without funding and kept singing. 'Weathered' means ____.
explain: 仍持續唱歌表示撐過缺乏經費的時期；weather作動詞＝安然度過，funding＝經費。

subject: english
q: Repeated insults fueled the argument, making both sides angrier. 'Fueled' means ____.
explain: 雙方更生氣，表示爭執被加劇；fuel＝助長，intensify＝加劇，settle＝解決。

subject: english
q: The talks bridged the gap between the teams; they now agree. 'Bridged' means ____.
explain: 從有分歧到同意，表示縮小差距；bridge the gap＝彌合差距，conceal＝隱藏。

subject: english
q: Give Arun time to digest the report before asking his opinion. 'Digest' means ____.
explain: 先理解報告才能提出意見；digest在此＝消化、理解資訊，不是重寫或發布。

subject: english
q: A familiar meal routine anchored her hectic days, giving her stability. 'Anchored' means ____.
explain: 固定用餐習慣讓忙亂生活安定下來；anchor＝使穩定，hectic＝忙亂的，stability＝穩定。

subject: english
q: Staff screened the entries for copied work before judging them. 'Screened' means ____.
explain: 評選前先查有無抄襲，screen＝審查；entry＝參賽作品，不是已經排名。

subject: english
q: The review praised the acting but questioned the ending. Its approval was ____.
explain: 肯定演技卻質疑結尾，表示贊同有所保留；qualified＝有保留的，enthusiastic＝熱烈的，hostile＝敵意的。

subject: english
q: The change raised the score from 80 to 81 out of 100, a ____ improvement.
explain: 只提高一分，屬小幅改善；marginal＝微小的，steady＝穩定持續的，單次變化無法判斷持續性。

subject: english
q: Without giving evidence, the seller asserts that the vase is ancient. 'Asserts' means ____.
explain: 沒有證據仍斷言是真古物；assert＝肯定地聲稱，本身不代表查證成功。

subject: english
q: Lea dismissed the idea without discussing it. She ____ the idea.
explain: 未討論就dismiss，表示拒絕考慮；dismiss＝摒棄、駁回，不是延後處理。

subject: english
q: The pass mark was 60. Niko scored 61 and said he 'barely passed.' This description fits.
explain: 比及格線多一分是勉強及格；barely＝勉強、僅僅，barely passed仍表示通過。

subject: english
q: A play got equal praise and criticism. Its 'mixed reviews' express a shared negative opinion.
explain: mixed reviews＝褒貶不一的評論，不是共同負評；praise＝稱讚，criticism＝批評。

subject: english
q: A report calls the theft 'alleged'; no verdict is given. This wording confirms that the theft occurred.
explain: alleged＝被指稱的、尚未證實的，不能據此確認竊案已發生；verdict＝判決。

subject: english
q: Of 100 messages about the mural, 96 praised it. Describing the support as 'overwhelming' fits.
explain: 100則留言中96則稱讚，支持比例懸殊；overwhelming＝壓倒性的，mural＝壁畫，並不表示全數贊成。

subject: english
q: The plants grew better after watering increased. The gardener attributed their growth ____ the extra water.
explain: attribute A to B＝把A歸因於B，生長是結果，增加的水是所認定的原因。

subject: english
q: The room had nowhere to sit, so donors furnished it ____ chairs.
explain: furnish a place with something＝為某處提供設備；房間是接受椅子的場所，donor＝捐贈者。

subject: english
q: The two bird calls sound alike. A recording helps us distinguish one ____ the other.
explain: distinguish A from B＝區分A與B；此處以錄音辨認兩種相似鳥鳴，call＝鳴叫聲。

subject: english
q: The parcel went to the wrong island because its label was missing. The missing label resulted ____ this error.
explain: because已明示缺少標籤是原因、誤送是結果；result in＝導致，result from＝起因於，因果方向相反。

subject: english
q: Staff reserve the front seats ____ guests who need extra legroom.
explain: reserve something for someone＝為某人保留某物；本句主詞staff是執行者，guests是受益者；legroom＝腿部空間。

subject: english
q: Loose wires could ____ a threat to workers walking through the workshop.
explain: pose a threat to＝對……構成威脅；loose wires＝鬆脫的電線。其他動詞不構成此搭配。

subject: english
q: Before choosing seeds, I consulted the farmer about the soil. 'About' correctly introduces the topic.
explain: consult someone about something＝就某事請教某人；farmer是請教對象，soil＝土壤，是議題。

subject: english
q: The bakery supplies bread to schools. Here, 'to schools' identifies where the bakery gets its bread.
explain: supply＝供應；supply bread to schools表示供應麵包給學校，to指出接受者，並非來源。

subject: english
q: The tent is too small, so we ruled it out for the trip. We ____.
explain: 因帳篷太小而rule it out＝排除這個選項；不是暫存、檢查或選用。

subject: english
q: The guide touched on local farming, then spent an hour on pottery. The farming topic was ____.
explain: touch on＝簡略提及；與後面花一小時談陶藝形成篇幅對比，pottery＝陶藝。

subject: english
q: As the cheers faded, excitement gave way to disappointment. What happened?
explain: A give way to B＝A被B取代，所以興奮轉為失望；fade＝漸弱。

subject: english
q: 'I work tonight. Can I take a rain check on dinner?' The speaker wants to ____.
explain: take a rain check＝改日再接受邀請；今晚工作是無法赴約的原因，與查天氣無關。

subject: english
q: The missing payment came to light during the review. This means the review kept the payment secret.
explain: come to light＝被發現、曝光；查核使漏款事件浮現，並非保密，payment＝款項。

subject: english
q: 'Fine,' he said, avoiding my eyes. Reading between the lines may reveal feelings he did not state.
explain: read between the lines＝領會言外之意；避開目光可作推論線索，may沒有斷言他必定生氣。

subject: english
q: Aya changes her route when roads close. Her travel plans show ____.
explain: 能隨封路調整行程是彈性；show後需名詞flexibility＝彈性，flexible是形容詞。

subject: english
q: Bo counts every bead twice. His work is marked by ____.
explain: 反覆清點顯示精確；by後需名詞precision＝精確，precise＝精確的，precisely＝精確地。

subject: english
q: A new ramp lets wheelchairs enter. It makes the hall more ____.
explain: 坡道讓輪椅可進入，make＋受詞＋形容詞，故用accessible＝可進入的；ramp＝坡道。

subject: english
q: The fee is hidden in small print. The ad does not state it ____.
explain: 費用藏在小字中，未清楚說明；修飾state用副詞clearly＝清楚地，clarity＝清晰。

subject: english
q: The three conflicting dates on the notice were ____ to readers.
explain: 日期衝突使讀者困惑，confusing to readers＝令讀者困惑的；confused通常搭配about，表示感到困惑。

subject: english
q: The survey left out night workers. Their ____ weakened its findings.
explain: 夜班工作者被排除，their後需名詞exclusion＝排除；exclude是動詞，exclusive是形容詞。

subject: english
q: The scale gives different weights for the same stone. 'Unreliable' is a suitable description of the scale.
explain: 同一石頭測出不同重量，故秤不可靠；unreliable＝不可靠的，un-在此表否定。

subject: english
q: The loss made the players lose hope. 'The players felt discouraging' correctly describes their feelings.
explain: 球員感到灰心應用discouraged；discouraging＝令人灰心的，描述引發感受的人事物。

subject: english
q: I began tending this garden in May and still do it daily. Since May, I ____ it.
explain: 從五月持續到現在，用現在完成進行式；have been tending＝一直照料，過去完成式須另有過去基準。

subject: english
q: The painter arrives tomorrow; work has not started. The room ____ yet.
explain: 截至現在尚未動工，用has not been painted＝尚未被粉刷；房間接受動作，had not been painted則須另有過去基準。

subject: english
q: Last Monday, we thought the boat would arrive that Friday. The arrival is presented as ____.
choices: a future event viewed from today
a future event viewed from Monday
explain: 上週一是過去的思考時間，以當時為基準，該週五尚未到來；would arrive＝從過去觀點看將抵達。

subject: english
q: Ona still works here. She joined in June. 'She had worked here since June' correctly states this at present.
explain: 敘述延續到現在應為has worked；had worked須有過去參照點，since June＝自六月以來。

subject: english
q: The curator packed the vase herself before noon. Which report matches?
choices: The vase was packed by the curator before noon.
The curator received a packed vase before noon.
The vase will be packed by the curator before noon.
The curator had someone pack the vase before noon.
explain: herself表親自打包，花瓶是受事者；was packed by＝被……打包，curator＝策展人；另三項改變角色、時間或執行者。

subject: english
q: The keys were copied by a locksmith for Ivo. This sentence identifies the locksmith as the person who copied them.
explain: by引出執行複製的人；locksmith＝鎖匠，for Ivo表示為Ivo製作，並非Ivo親自複製。

subject: english
q: The chef to ____ we recommended this market now buys fish there.
explain: 把市場推薦給主廚，主廚是to的受詞；先行詞為人，介系詞後用whom，chef＝主廚。

subject: english
q: This is the tiny brush with ____ the artist paints dots on shells.
explain: 畫家用這支刷子畫點，with表示工具；物的關係代名詞用which，shell＝貝殼。

subject: english
q: I chose another solution. Still, I thanked Ada. Join: I thanked Ada ____ I chose another solution.
explain: 雖選別的方法仍道謝，是讓步關係；even though＝雖然，so that＝為了，as soon as＝一……就。

subject: english
q: Keep the stage lights off until the music starts. This instruction means turning them on before the music starts.
explain: until＝直到，燈須維持關閉到音樂開始，不能解讀為開始前就開燈；stage lights＝舞臺燈。

subject: english
q: The team learned local history by ____ older residents about their childhood.
explain: by後接動名詞表示方法；interviewing＝訪談，團隊透過訪問居民了解地方歷史。

subject: english
q: Our duties include sorting donated clothes and ____ torn pockets.
explain: and連接同為duties內容的兩項活動，需與sorting並列用mending＝修補；pocket＝口袋。

subject: english
q: We mapped old wells instead of digging new ones. 'Digging' is correctly used after 'instead of.'
explain: instead of後可接動名詞，digging形式正確；instead of＝而非，well＝水井。

subject: english
q: We sold stones ____ by sand and waves; the sea had smoothed their edges.
explain: 石頭被砂與海浪磨光，用過去分詞polished修飾；polish＝磨光，edge＝邊緣。

subject: english
q: The woman translating the menu asked about a dish. Here, 'translating' says someone else was translating for her.
explain: translating＝正在翻譯，主動修飾woman，表示她親自翻譯；不是別人替她翻譯。

subject: english
q: Jin knew how to fix the wheel but waited for help. Which phrase describes his unused ability?
explain: 問的是未使用的能力，could have fixed it＝當時本可修好；cannot have與must have表對過去的推測，非此處重點。

subject: english
q: 'Did Vera label the jars?' 'She meant to, but forgot.' What did Vera intend to do?
explain: meant to後省略label the jars，表示原本打算貼標籤；intend＝打算，jar＝罐子。

subject: english
q: I ordered the rice spicy, but the soup mild. Here, 'mild' describes how I wanted the rice.
explain: 後半省略I ordered，mild是the soup的受詞補語，指湯的口味；spicy＝辣的，mild＝清淡的。

subject: english
q: Nell replaced long forms with one checkbox. This saved visitors time. 'This' refers to ____.
explain: this回指把冗長表單改成單一勾選框的做法；simplify＝簡化，checkbox＝勾選框。

subject: english
q: Rui stored ripe plums beside empty bowls. They would spoil by Monday. 'They' refers to ____.
explain: 會腐壞的是熟李子，不是距離they最近的碗；plum＝李子，spoil＝腐壞。

subject: english
q: A tailor met a sailor near the dock. The clothing maker waved. Who waved?
explain: clothing maker＝做衣服的人，承接tailor＝裁縫；sailor＝水手，不是新增第三個人物。

subject: english
q: Several notes criticized the price; one praised it. The positive comment came last. Which came last?
choices: A note asking for a price.
explain: positive comment＝正面評論，對應praised the price＝稱讚價格；不是批評或詢價。

subject: english
q: Tao and his sister rented bikes. Only hers had a basket. Which bike had a basket?
explain: hers是所有格代名詞，指his sister的腳踏車；basket＝籃子，only表示只有她那輛有。

subject: english
q: Eli gave Pia two plans, but she rejected both. 'Both' refers to the two plans.
explain: rejected的受詞both承接two plans，指兩個方案，不是兩名人物；reject＝拒絕。

subject: english
q: Old jeans become bags at our workshop. Even damaged pockets find a second use here. Best heading?
explain: 兩句都在談舊衣再利用，故以新用途為主題；jeans＝牛仔褲，a second use＝再次利用。

subject: english
q: Some rooms serve two purposes daily. One becomes a kitchen after morning art lessons. The second sentence ____.
choices: gives an example of the first
gives a reason to cancel art
explain: 同一房間先上美術課再當廚房，是兩種用途的具體例子；purpose＝用途，example＝例證。

subject: english
q: P: Bea lifted the lid of the wooden box. Q: Its hands had stopped at noon. Insert: 'Inside, she found a clock.'
choices: It does not fit the passage.
explain: 先開盒發現時鐘，後句its hands才有明確指涉；lid＝蓋子，hands在此＝時針與分針。

subject: english
q: A cafe repairs cups instead of replacing them. It also reuses jars for storing sugar. Best conclusion?
choices: The cafe tries to reduce its waste.
The cafe makes its own cups.
explain: 修理杯子與重複使用罐子都能減少廢棄物；reduce its waste 在此指減少咖啡館產生的廢棄物。文中無法推知罐子受損、不買糖或自行製作杯子。

subject: english
q: Mina could not hear train announcements clearly. A screen now displays each message in large letters. Pattern?
choices: Two causes of the same problem.
explain: 先呈現聽不清的問題，再提出大字螢幕方案；announcement＝公告，solution＝解決方法。

subject: english
q: Market stalls once used different tokens. Now all accept the same kind. 'Simpler Payments' is a suitable heading.
explain: 從各攤各用一種代幣，改為共用一種，支付更簡便；stall＝攤位，token＝代幣，payment＝支付。

subject: english
q: The guide offers tips for indoor plants. Its example covers repairing fences outside. The example supports the topic.
explain: 修戶外圍籬無法支持室內養植物的建議，例證離題；indoor＝室內的，fence＝圍籬。

subject: english
q: Six volunteers tasted the new menu and liked it. What does this tell us?
choices: The old menu was less popular.
Customers would pay more for it.
explain: 證據只涵蓋六位試吃者的喜好，未比較舊菜單或調查付費意願；volunteer＝志願者，taster＝試吃者。

subject: english
q: The gadget is clever, yet I would wait for longer trials. The writer is ____.
explain: clever是肯定，wait for longer trials表示仍審慎；gadget＝小裝置，cautious＝謹慎的。

subject: english
q: Ira kept the receipt but skipped registration. Free repairs require both. Which follows?
choices: Ira has not met the repair requirements.
Ira no longer owns the product.
explain: 免費維修同時要求收據與登記，缺登記就不符；receipt＝收據，registration＝登記。

subject: english
q: A seller claims its cloth holds more water per square cm. Which comparison with a rival cloth tests this?
choices: Water held by soaked pieces of equal area.
Total wet weight of pieces of equal area.
Dry weight of pieces of equal area.
Water held by pieces of equal thickness.
explain: 每平方公分的吸水量要控制布面積，再比吸收的水重；濕布總重含原布重，不能當吸水量。area＝面積。

subject: english
q: Noise fell from 60 to 40 units. Sleep was not measured. Which claim lacks support?
explain: 只量噪音，未量睡眠，不能判斷睡得更好；lack support＝缺乏支持，decrease＝下降。

subject: english
q: Only weekday users were surveyed. Their views describe the sample, but weekend users may differ.
explain: 只訪問平日使用者，週末族群可能有不同看法；sample＝樣本，survey＝調查。

subject: english
q: Groups using lamps A and B read at the same speed. This provides some evidence that B enables faster reading than A.
explain: 兩組讀速相同，沒有支持B燈比A燈讀得更快的證據；at the same speed＝以相同速度，evidence＝證據。

subject: english
q: Chess 10:00; drama 10:30; choir 11:00. Each lasts 30 min. May stays 10:20–11:00. Which full session fits?
explain: 戲劇10:30至11:00全落在停留時間內；棋類已開始，合唱在離開時才開始。drama＝戲劇，choir＝合唱。

subject: english
q: From the gate go east to the hut, north to the pond, then west to the tower. At the pond, you ____.
explain: 抵達池塘時面向北，要往西須左轉；hut＝小屋，pond＝池塘，tower＝塔。

subject: english
q: Packing: 9:00; sealing: 9:20; loading: 9:50. The gap after sealing is longer than the gap before it.
explain: 封口前一段20分鐘，後一段30分鐘，後段較長；sealing＝封口，loading＝裝載。

subject: english
q: Relative to a well: shed west, gate east, field south. The shed and field are on opposite sides of the well.
explain: 西與南不是相反方向；相對兩側是西側棚屋與東側大門。well＝水井，shed＝棚屋。

subject: english
q: These tools travel well but break easily. Their ____ is poor.
explain: 易壞代表耐用性差，their後需名詞durability＝耐用性；portability＝便攜性，與優點相符而非缺點。

subject: english
q: Buses run often but rarely arrive on time. Service is frequent but lacks ____.
explain: 班次多卻不準時，缺的是punctuality＝準時，且lacks後需名詞；frequency＝頻率，punctual＝準時的。

subject: english
q: Students chose to join; paid staff were required to attend. Only the students participated ____.
explain: 學生自行選擇，職員必須出席；修飾participated須用副詞voluntarily＝自願地；compulsorily＝強制地。

subject: english
q: A kiosk sells tickets quickly but offers no event details. Its service is ____.
explain: 售票快速對應efficient＝有效率的；此處用形容詞描述服務特性。informative＝提供資訊的，不符未提供活動細節的材料。

subject: english
q: Writers choose topics alone but edit together. 'Topic choice is independent; editing is cooperative' is a valid summary.
explain: 自行選題、共同編輯，分別對應independent＝獨立的及cooperative＝合作的；摘要的名詞與形容詞配置也正確。

subject: english
q: Ana: 'Fewer boxes, please.' Bo: 'Reuse the wrapping.' Both want to ____.
explain: 少用盒子、重用包裝都減少包裝消耗；cut back on＝減少，兩人未討論成本或增加包裝空間。

subject: english
q: Cai: 'The pay is low.' Dev: 'Yes, but the hours suit me.' They see eye to eye on ____.
explain: Dev的yes認同薪水低，但工時合適只是Dev的看法；see eye to eye＝意見一致，pay＝薪資。

subject: english
q: Uma: 'No ride before a battery check.' Wes: 'Check the brakes before riding.' Both favor ____.
explain: 兩人都主張先檢查再騎，符合play it safe＝謹慎行事；沒有趕進度、固定時程或練習的資訊。

subject: english
q: Paz: 'The launch should be today.' Gil: 'I agree; training can wait.' They agree to hold off on the launch.
explain: 兩人都贊成今天推出，延後的是訓練；hold off on＝延後，launch＝推出，與題目摘要相反。

subject: english
q: Staff planned to inspect rooms Friday but did so the following Monday. Which summary is correct?
choices: The staff were inspected before the planned date.
The rooms were inspected after the planned date.
The rooms were inspected before the planned date.
The staff were inspected after the planned date.
explain: 實際下週一晚於原定週五，且被檢查的是房間；were inspected＝被檢查，following＝接下來的。

subject: english
q: Lea sent the forms Tuesday. Staff are checking them now. Which summary keeps both events?
choices: The forms were sent Tuesday and have been checked.
The forms were checked Tuesday and are being sent.
The forms were being checked Tuesday and were then sent.
The forms were sent Tuesday and are being checked.
explain: were sent＝被寄出，表週二完成的動作；are being checked＝正被查核；have been checked則表已完成。

subject: english
q: The bridge was tested May 2 and opened May 5. 'It had been tested before it opened' preserves the order.
explain: 先檢測再開放，過去完成被動had been tested可標明開放前已完成；preserve the order＝保留順序。

subject: english
q: A queue grows with one clerk. A second clerk starts serving, and waits fall. Best topic sentence?
choices: Waiting times fall when more clerks serve customers.
Waiting times rise when more clerks serve customers.
Waiting times fall when more clerks to serve customers.
Waiting times rise when more clerks to serve customers.
explain: 增員後等候變短，用fall；when後須完整子句，故用clerks serve，不能用to serve；queue＝隊伍。

subject: english
q: A garden grows crops needing shade and crops needing sun. Which topic sentence fits?
choices: Gardeners need spots what offer different light levels.
Gardeners need spots what offer the same light level.
Gardeners need spots that offer different light levels.
Gardeners need spots that offer the same light level.
explain: 兩類作物需要不同光照；spots後用that引導關係子句，不能用what；shade＝遮蔭處，sun＝陽光。

subject: english
q: The shelter's first beds are ready at a factory. A truck will ____ them to the shelter.
explain: 工廠備妥床鋪，卡車要把它們運到收容所，因此用 deliver（運送）；store 是存放，unpack 是拆開包裝。

subject: english
q: During the magic act, Nia hands the magician each prop. She is his ____.
explain: Nia 在表演中遞道具，扮演 assistant（助手）；spectator 是觀眾，sponsor 是贊助者，都不是協助演出的角色。

subject: english
q: To find songs by mood, Lian is ____ each recording with words such as 'calm' or 'lively'.
explain: 用情緒關鍵字標記錄音，方便日後搜尋，應用 tagging（加標籤）；rating 是評分，timing 是計時。

subject: english
q: The stage was dark, but a spotlight made the dancer's face clearly ____.
explain: 聚光燈讓原本黑暗中的臉看得見，visible 意為「可見的」；familiar 是熟悉的，vacant 是空著的。

subject: english
q: After the syrup spilled, the counter felt ____, and paper scraps clung to it.
explain: 紙屑黏在灑過糖漿的檯面上，對應 sticky（黏的）；slippery 是滑的，不能解釋紙屑黏住的線索。

subject: english
q: The diary was written by one of Inez's ____, who lived six generations before her.
explain: 比 Inez 早六代的家人是 ancestors（祖先）；descendants 是後代，siblings 是兄弟姊妹，世代方向不同。

subject: english
q: The council posts a housing plan for public comment before approval. Calling the plan a 'draft' fits.
explain: 尚未核定、供公眾提供意見的計畫可稱 draft（草案），並非已正式通過的版本；approval 是核准。

subject: english
q: The market began outdoors, then moved into a hall. Describing it as 'initially indoors' fits.
explain: initially 是「起初」。市場起初在戶外，後來才搬入室內，因此 initially indoors（起初在室內）把時間先後弄反。

subject: english
q: Cracks make a cliff potentially dangerous. The warning describes a risk even though a collapse has not occurred.
explain: potentially 是「可能地、潛在地」；裂縫帶來崩塌風險，即使尚未崩塌，也可稱 potentially dangerous（有潛在危險的）。

subject: english
q: The tenant keeps shared areas tidy and handles disputes calmly. Neighbors find her ____.
explain: 她維持公共區域整潔，平和處理爭執，顯示 agreeable（好相處的）；obedient 是服從命令，題文沒有上下級要求。

subject: english
q: The tent's ____ cost included its purchase price and every repair over its ten-year life.
explain: eventual 是「最終的」，此處費用合計購買與十年間的全部維修；initial（最初的）、partial（部分的）、monthly（每月的）都不符總支出的範圍。

subject: english
q: No such program existed until a student ____ one, inviting others to a weekly silent lunch.
explain: 原先沒有這項活動，學生首次發起它，應用 initiated（發起）；inherited 是繼承，abolished 是廢除，皆預設已有事物。

subject: english
q: After a second bakery opened, competition ____, forcing both shops to cut prices.
explain: 新店加入迫使兩店降價，顯示競爭 intensified（加劇）；faded 是減弱，settled 是平息，與後文的壓力不合。

subject: english
q: This case protects a lens in extreme cold; it can ____ temperatures that crack ordinary plastic.
explain: 保護盒能耐受會使普通塑膠裂開的低溫，tolerate 指「承受、耐受」；measure 是測量，generate 是產生。

subject: english
q: Mara offered help only while cameras were on. Her sudden departure made us doubt her ____.
explain: 只在鏡頭前幫忙，令人懷疑她是否真心，故為 sincerity（真誠）；authority 是權威，identity 是身分。

subject: english
q: A report says the tunnel is dry, but fresh photographs ____ that claim by showing water inside.
explain: 照片拍到積水，與「隧道乾燥」相反，counter 作動詞意為「反駁」；confirm（證實）及 echo（附和）會弄反證據方向。

subject: english
q: A cargo list groups plums and onions under 'produce'. Here, 'produce' names ____.
explain: plums（李子）與 onions（洋蔥）屬農產品；produce 在清單中是名詞「農產品」，不是動詞「生產」。

subject: english
q: A 'supposedly silent' motor turns out to roar. 'Supposedly' reports the writer's verified finding.
explain: supposedly 是「據稱、按理說」，轉述尚未獲確認的說法；馬達實際很吵，不能把原先的安靜宣稱當作作者查證的結論。

subject: english
q: Each trainee must attend the safety drill to pass the course. Attendance is ____.
explain: 必須參加安全演練才能通過課程，故 compulsory 是「強制的」；voluntary（自願的）與 must 的義務要求相反，drill 指演練。

subject: english
q: A leak creates a grave risk to the archive. Here, 'grave' is an adjective meaning serious.
explain: grave 作形容詞可指「嚴重的」，不只作名詞「墳墓」；漏水可能毀掉檔案，符合嚴重危機的語境。

subject: english
q: The missing final chord sent the composer on a ____ to find the song's original ending.
explain: go on a quest for／to find 表示「展開尋找」；quest 是探索、尋求，適合為了補回歌曲結尾而追查的情境。

subject: english
q: Nora joined a debate to build confidence, not to win. She took part for reasons ____ victory.
explain: Nora 參賽是為了建立信心，並非追求 victory（勝利），故用 other than（除了……以外）；related to 則是「與……有關」，不符語意。

subject: english
q: One missed booking could spell disaster for the tiny touring band. This means it could cause serious trouble.
explain: spell disaster 是「招致災難、造成嚴重後果」；此處 spell 不是拼字，指漏掉預約可能重創小型巡演樂團。

subject: english
q: By noon, spam had filled the inbox and blocked new messages. The inbox was ____ spam.
explain: be choked with 表示「被……塞滿、堵住」；垃圾郵件阻擋新信，符合此義，credited with 則是被歸功於。

subject: english
q: The runner came close to the record, but not quite. This says the runner matched the record.
explain: but not quite 是「但還差一點」，表示接近卻未達成；matched the record（追平紀錄）則表示已達成。

subject: english
q: Decades later, the rule still works in every trial. It has ____ the test of time.
explain: stand the test of time 是「經得起時間考驗」；數十年後仍有效正是此義，完成式用 stood，不能套用 take a test（應試）。

subject: english
q: Dan falsely said he composed Mei's winning tune, taking ____ for her work.
explain: take credit for 是「把功勞歸給自己」；Dan 冒稱是得獎曲作者，正是攬功，blame 則指應受責備的責任。

subject: english
q: With its roof damaged, a theater made an ____ for carpenters to volunteer.
explain: make an appeal for 表示「呼籲、請求」；劇院屋頂損壞而徵求木工志工，並非提出 excuse（藉口）或 estimate（估價）。

subject: english
q: The robot turns toward even a faint clap, showing that it is highly ____ sound.
explain: responsive to 是「對……有反應的」；連輕微拍手也會引起轉向，不能用 indifferent to（對……漠不關心的）。

subject: english
q: In batches of 100 parcels each, labeling errors fell from six to one, an ____ in accuracy.
explain: 每批皆有100件，貼錯由六降為一，表示 accuracy（準確性）提升；an 後接名詞 improvement（改善），不是 impairment（損害），也不能接 improving。

subject: english
q: Two bakers improved one recipe: one reduced salt, the other changed flour. Their achievement was ____.
explain: 兩人共同改良同一配方，成就是 collective（集體的），不是 individual（個人的）；兩個 -ly 形式是副詞，不能作此處的形容詞補語。

subject: english
q: A lab uses new scanners but keeps its founder's old measuring methods. It blends innovation with ____.
explain: 新儀器與創辦人的舊方法共存，對應 innovation（創新）與 tradition（傳統）；with 後須接名詞，replacement（取代）也不符保留舊法。

subject: english
q: Since last winter, neighbors ____ night skies weekly, and the project is still growing.
explain: since last winter 連結過去起點與現在持續的觀測，使用現在完成進行式 have been recording（一直在記錄）；過去完成式需另有過去基準。

subject: english
q: In 1998, an inventor predicted her tool would become common. The expected popularity comes before her prediction.
explain: would become 表示「從過去看未來」，預測的普及時間在 1998 年之後；此時態不保證工具後來真的普及。common 是普遍的。

subject: english
q: The rescue team found the address to ____ the supplies had been sent.
explain: send supplies to an address（把物資送到某地址）的 to 被移到關係代名詞前，形成 to which；where 不能在此與 to 疊用。

subject: english
q: ____ with thick gloves, the volunteers handled the rough wood safely.
explain: volunteers（志工）是被提供手套的人，與 equip（配備）為被動關係，故用 Equipped；主動分詞 equipping 需要說明配備誰。

subject: english
q: A robot repairs bikes damaged in transit. 'Damaged' describes something that happened to the bikes.
explain: damaged（受損的）是過去分詞，修飾接受損壞結果的 bikes（自行車），不是說自行車主動損壞其他東西；in transit 指運送途中。

subject: english
q: Ada had time for a free tour but stayed home. Which phrase describes her missed opportunity?
explain: could have joined it 表示「當時本可參加」；stayed home（待在家）才交代她沒參加。must have joined it 則是推測她已參加。

subject: english
q: A courier route once linked remote clinics. ____. Walkers now follow it to learn local history.
choices: It was built to host modern art shows.
It now takes medicine across the sea.
It has since become a heritage trail.
It has remained a private medical route.
explain: 原先連接診所，如今供人步行了解歷史，中間須交代路線用途的轉變；heritage trail 是「文化歷史步道」，不是繼續作私人醫療路線。

subject: english
q: At a repair fair, volunteers fix lamps. ____ These services keep useful items out of landfills.
explain: These services（這些服務）承接修燈與 mend（修補）書包，兩者都延長物品壽命、減少送入 landfills（掩埋場）的廢棄物；添購新品不屬修繕。

subject: english
q: A guide calls a dancer's shoes 'a second skin.' The phrase mainly explains how the shoes are manufactured.
explain: a second skin（第二層皮膚）比喻鞋與舞者密不可分、貼合自然；它強調關係，不是在說明鞋子的製造流程。

subject: english
q: A seed packet says 'Bury 1 cm deep; water twice weekly; harvest in June.' Which detail is missing?
choices: How deep to sow the seeds.
How often to water the seeds.
How much sunlight the plants need.
explain: 包裝提供播種深度、每週澆水兩次及六月收成，沒有 sunlight（日照）需求。sow 是播種，harvest 是收成；不可把未寫的資訊當成已提供。

subject: english
q: A stone arch marks the harbor. Ships sail past the monument daily. 'The monument' refers to the arch.
explain: 文中的 stone arch（石拱門）被接著稱為 the monument（紀念建物）；這是同一物件的替代稱呼，並非指來往的 ships（船隻）。

subject: english
q: An umbrella kept its user dry in one windy shower. Its maker expects ten years of use. Which claim lacks test support?
explain: 一次有風陣雨已測到風吹、淋雨及當次遮雨效果，卻不足以證明能用 a decade（十年）；expects（預期）不是十年耐用性的測試證據。

subject: english
q: Sana wove and sold bags before emigrating; Hugo emigrated, then learned weaving and sold his work. Both ____.
choices: received training in the same country.
explain: 兩人都販售自己的編織品，因此都由 weaving（編織）獲得收入；Hugo 在 abroad（國外）才學習，不能推成兩人都在移居前學習或開賣。

subject: english
q: Critics said the bell had never rung. ____, recordings later revealed its sound during past festivals.
explain: never rung（從未響過）的說法與後來錄音中的鐘聲相反，須用 However（然而）表示轉折；不是例證、因果或相同情況。

subject: english
q: A coach credits talent to heredity but says lessons build skill too. Which sentence links these ideas?
choices: Family traits influence skill through lessons.
Both inheritance and experience shape skill.
Talent grows as relatives attend more lessons.
explain: 教練同時談 heredity（遺傳）與 lessons（課程），摘要須納入 inheritance（遺傳）及 experience（後天經驗）；不是說技能決定遺傳特徵。

subject: english
q: Shade screens protect museum fabrics from fading. The text gives keeping visitors cool as the reason for the screens.
explain: 題文說遮光幕用來防止 fabrics（布料）fading（褪色）；敘述把保護藏品的目的換成讓遊客涼快，並無文字依據。

subject: english
q: The troupe delays rehearsal until its translator returns. It waits for the translator before rehearsing.
explain: 劇團延後排練，直到翻譯人員回來，表示等她回來才開始；troupe 是劇團，rehearsal 是排練，不能把等待誤讀成照常先開始。

subject: english
q: The theater club opened in 1990; the film club began thirty years earlier. Which is older?
explain: thirty years earlier（早三十年）以戲劇社成立為基準，故電影社較早成立；只須掌握 earlier 的方向，不必算出年份。

subject: english
q: Kai: 'The shoes rub.' Lin: 'The soles wear out fast.' Both comments mainly concern the shoes' appearance.
explain: rub 指鞋子磨腳，談舒適度；wear out fast 指鞋底很快磨損，談耐用度。兩則評論並非主要談 appearance（外觀）。

subject: english
q: Nia: 'I'd rent it if insurance is included.' Omar: 'I won't rent it, even with cover.' Who accepts conditionally?
explain: Nia 願在附 insurance（保險）的條件下承租，屬有條件接受；Omar 連有保障也拒租。conditionally 是「有條件地」。

subject: english
q: Workers freeze berries, then dry them under low pressure. This process preserves their shape. What is 'this process'?
choices: Freezing the berries without drying them.
Drying the berries before freezing them.
Drying the berries at high pressure.
explain: this process（這個過程）回指先冷凍、再低壓乾燥的整套步驟；不能只取冷凍，或把順序與壓力條件倒置。

subject: english
q: P: Fossils arrive. Q: Talks and films teach. R: Fees rise. S: Doors close. 'Learning takes many forms' summarizes ____.
explain: Q 列出 talks（講座）與 films（影片）兩種學習方式，適合用 Learning takes many forms（學習有多種形式）統整；其他段落談標本、費用或關門。

subject: english
q: A buoy shows two white bands above one black band. Which description matches it from top to bottom?
explain: above 是「在……上方」，故由上到下先兩條白帶、再一條黑帶；buoy 指浮標，應依文字順序配對，不靠圖片。

subject: english
q: P: Bags tore. Q: A stronger weave emerged. R: Shops abroad adopted it. S: Sales fell. 'The design spread' sums up ____.
explain: R 的海外店家 adopted（採用）新織法，可歸納為 The design spread（這項設計傳播開來）；Q 只介紹更強韌的織法，abroad 是在國外。

subject: english
q: Solar lamps cut fuel use. However, cloudy weeks can leave paths dark. The writer organizes ideas by ____.
choices: explaining the steps of a repair
comparing a benefit with a drawback
explain: 先說省燃料的 benefit（優點），再以 However 引入陰天照明不足的 drawback（缺點）；不是年代排序或維修程序。

subject: english
q: Ari: 'A tool library deserves funding.' Bea: 'Its value does not justify its cost.' Who supports the library?
explain: Ari 主張值得撥款，表達支持；Bea 認為效益不足以 justify（使合理化）成本，表達反對，不能因提到 value 就判為贊同。

subject: english
q: A tailor puts buttons beside coats, then uses needles to sew them onto the cuffs. 'Them' refers to ____.
explain: 縫到 cuffs（袖口）上的物件是 buttons（鈕扣）；needles（針）是工具，coats（外套）是衣物，不能只選離 them 最近的複數名詞。

subject: english
q: Club A lends tents; B fixes boots; C rents cameras; D sells shoes. Jo needs boots repaired and a tent loan. Which pair?
explain: boots（靴子）要修理，對應 B；tent loan（借用帳篷）對應 A。須同時滿足需求，D 只賣鞋，不能把購買誤當成修理服務。

Several spent long periods studying their boards without speaking; he kept his own hands off their pieces. When a boy made an unsuccessful move, Theo asked what he had been trying to achieve. After listening, he helped the boy __4__ his move. The boy took it back and found a safer square. A comfortable hotel bed can still produce a restless night. Travelers may blame the pillow, but sleep researchers have another possibility to consider: the room itself is unfamiliar. This difficulty on the first night in a new setting is so common that scientists have given it a name, the first-night effect.
To investigate it, a research team measured brain activity while volunteers slept in a laboratory. During the first period of deep sleep, one region on the left side showed signs of lighter sleep than the matching region on the right. The left side also responded more strongly to unusual sounds, which could wake the sleepers. On a later night in the laboratory, the differences between the two sides were much smaller. These observations suggested that the brain's response could change as the place became more familiar.
The researchers suggest that part of the brain may stand guard while a person rests in a new place. Yet their measurements covered a particular brain network during an early sleep period. They do not show that an entire half of the brain remains awake all night. The findings also help explain a common laboratory practice: researchers often give volunteers an adjustment night before collecting the sleep records they intend to study. Without that chance to settle in, the records might show a response to the laboratory rather than the person's usual sleep.

Measuring Usual Sleep from a Single Night

Are frozen vegetables a poor substitute for fresh ones? The word fresh sounds like a guarantee, but it tells shoppers little about the time between harvest and dinner. Fresh vegetables may spend days in transport, on a store shelf, and in a home refrigerator. During that period, amounts of some vitamins can decline. A comparison made at harvest may therefore differ from one made when the food reaches a plate.
Does freezing protect everything? Before freezing, many vegetables are briefly heated in water or steam. This step slows the activity of enzymes, substances that can cause changes in color and flavor. Heating can also lead to some vitamin loss, especially when it continues too long. Freezing then helps preserve what remains. Studies comparing stored fresh and frozen produce have found that the winner varies with the vegetable and the vitamin measured. Similar amounts of one vitamin do not guarantee similar amounts of another.
What should a shopper do with this information? Start with a realistic meal plan. Someone cooking tonight may enjoy fresh vegetables bought that morning. Someone whose schedule changes often may find a frozen bag more useful, since portions can be taken out as needed. To retain nutrients, follow storage and cooking directions rather than judging the food by its package. A vegetable's condition when eaten deserves more attention than the label it carried when purchased.
q: What is the main purpose of this question-and-answer text?
choices: To favor produce with shorter transport times.
To show why heating improves vitamin levels.
To rank vegetables by their vitamin content.
To guide choices between fresh and frozen food.

subject: english
passage:
In 1816, a French doctor faced a difficulty that a modern medical instrument would make easy to overlook. Rene Laennec wanted to listen to a young woman's heart. Placing his ear directly against her chest seemed improper to him. He rolled paper into a tube, placed one end against her chest, and listened through the other. The heart sounds were distinct enough to make this simple arrangement worth exploring.
Laennec developed a wooden version of the tube, which became known as the stethoscope. Paper had allowed a quick experiment; wood provided an instrument that could be used repeatedly. Yet making a tube was just one part of his achievement. He studied the sounds heard during examinations and connected them with changes found inside diseased bodies. Listening could supply clues that an examination of the body's surface might miss. Those clues became useful through repeated observation and comparison.
Seen in a museum case, an early wooden stethoscope may look less impressive than the machines found in hospitals today. Its importance lies in the new practice that developed around it. A doctor had to learn which sounds mattered and what they might indicate. Clearer access to a sound did not make its meaning obvious. The object therefore records two kinds of work: creating a way to hear inside the body and developing the knowledge needed to interpret what was heard.
q: Which title best suits this passage?
choices: A Simple Tube and a New Way to Examine Patients
Why Clear Heart Sounds Replaced Medical Judgment
From Reusable Wooden Tubes to Modern Machines
How Social Customs Determined a Tube's Material
explain: 全文由紙筒、木製聽診器談到新的診療方式，主旨涵蓋工具與運用；雖提到現代機器，並未追述木筒如何演變成現代機器。

subject: english
passage:
Dear Editor, Your magazine often explains how to read health claims. I suggest devoting an article to the people who disappear from a study's final report. Suppose an advertisement for a skin cream says that most users improved during a trial. The claim sounds encouraging, but the small print limits it to the people who completed the trial. It gives no information about those who left early. A reader could easily mistake a report about the remaining participants for a report about everyone who began.
People can withdraw for different reasons. Some may find regular visits inconvenient. Others may stop because the cream irritates their skin or because they see little improvement. Still others may feel better and decide further visits are unnecessary. These possibilities point in different directions. Without knowing why people left and what happened to them, we cannot simply assume their experience matched that of the people who stayed.
A future article could show readers where to look for the number of people who started, the number who finished, and the reasons recorded for leaving. It should also explain whether researchers continued collecting results after participants stopped using the cream. Counting everyone who leaves as a failure would hide important differences, just as leaving them out could make the remaining group misleading. Clear reporting would let readers judge how much trust a promising conclusion deserves.
q: What is the writer mainly asking the editor to do?
choices: Publish a comparison of popular skin creams.
Recommend fewer visits for trial participants.
Teach readers to examine missing trial results.
Explain why successful users leave trials early.
explain: 信件要求報導研究中途退出者與缺漏結果，教讀者判讀宣稱；「感到改善而退出」僅是第二段的一種可能，不能代表全文訴求。

subject: english
passage:
A fish that has disappeared from view may still leave a path behind it. As it swims, it disturbs the water, producing small movements that continue after it has passed. For a harbor seal, this temporary path can be useful. Its whiskers can pick up movements too slight for a human swimmer to notice. The fish itself does not have to touch the seal's face.
Researchers have explored this skill with a small remote-controlled machine in a pool. While the machine traveled, a trained seal waited with its eyes covered and its whiskers above the water. Headphones played noise to prevent it from hearing the motor. Once the machine stopped, the headphones were removed and the animal was allowed to search. The silent motor could no longer provide a sound cue. Still wearing its eye covering, the seal could follow the watery trail. The machine made it possible to repeat a route without relying on a live fish's unpredictable movements.
Such tests help explain how seals can hunt when visibility is poor. Yet the water is not a permanent record: a trail weakens over time, and rough currents can mix it with other movements. Whiskers therefore offer useful clues under suitable conditions. They give seals access to information that a person looking into an apparently empty pool might miss.
q: Which focus best describes this article?
choices: A hunting skill beyond a seal's eyesight.
A training method for keeping seals in pools.
The changing routes of fish in rough seas.
The value of sound when seals follow fish.
explain: 全文以水流痕跡、實驗與環境限制說明海豹視覺以外的獵食能力。訓練只是實驗手段，並非文章重點。

Dear Maya, you asked whether the birds at the bay were worth a visit. I went there hoping to photograph a flock rising together. From behind a wooden viewing screen, however, I saw mostly small birds walking through the mud. I nearly left. Then a volunteer lent me her field glasses, and I watched the birds pull tiny animals from the wet ground. These were travelers stopping between distant breeding and wintering grounds. A feeding stop, she explained, was part of their journey, not a break from it.
At low tide, the exposed mud supplied food that could become body fat, their fuel for the next long flight. When the sea covered it, the birds gathered on a nearby dry bank. They needed both places: one for feeding, the other for resting without spending much energy. A dog suddenly ran toward the bank, and the whole flock rose. The volunteer pointed out that repeated flights like this used up reserves the birds were trying to build.
As the flock settled, I stepped back behind the screen. This gave the birds more space while I continued watching. I still took photographs, but I no longer tried to make an exciting flight happen. If you join me next weekend, bring field glasses. We may see birds doing very little, and I now think that is a good reason to stay. Your sister, Nora.
q: What is Nora's main reason for writing?
choices: To compare stops along a bird migration route.
To explain a new approach to watching birds.
To recommend a site for dramatic flight photos.
To explain why the birds left the bay for winter.
explain: 信中從想拍群鳥起飛，轉為不驚擾地觀察，並邀對方同行。戲劇性飛行照片只是起初的期待，並非最後推薦的賞鳥方式。

Our town is considering a new charge for boats tied up in the bay. The money would replace some ordinary moorings with equipment designed to protect seagrass. Boat owners understandably ask why they should pay more for a place to stop. The answer lies beneath their boats, in a habitat that receives less attention than the beach.
Seagrass grows in shallow water, where its leaves shelter young fish and its roots help hold the bottom in place. At an ordinary mooring, a heavy chain may sweep across the seabed as a boat shifts with wind and current. Over time, the chain can leave circular scars in the meadow. The proposed systems hold the connecting line above the bottom, limiting this repeated scraping. They change how a boat is secured rather than asking its owner to abandon the bay.
Cost remains a fair concern. The town should begin with a small trial instead of charging everyone for an immediate replacement. Surveyors should record plant cover before installation and after a growing season, along with boat use and water conditions. A greener bottom means little as evidence for the equipment if most boats have simply gone elsewhere. Owners deserve a clear account of what their payments achieve. A trial would let the town examine whether protecting the meadow and keeping the bay useful can advance together.

Our town is considering a new charge for boats tied up in the bay. The money would replace some ordinary moorings with equipment designed to protect seagrass. Boat owners understandably ask why they should pay more for a place to stop. The answer lies beneath their boats, in a habitat that receives less attention than the beach.
Seagrass grows in shallow water, where its leaves shelter young fish and its roots help hold the bottom in place. At an ordinary mooring, a heavy chain may sweep across the seabed as a boat shifts with wind and current. Over time, the chain can leave circular scars in the meadow. The proposed systems hold the connecting line above the bottom, limiting this repeated scraping. They change how a boat is secured rather than asking its owner to abandon the bay.
Cost remains a fair concern. The town should begin with a small trial instead of charging everyone for an immediate replacement. Surveyors should record plant cover before installation and after a growing season, along with boat use and water conditions. A greener bottom means little as evidence for the equipment if most boats have simply gone elsewhere. Owners deserve a clear account of what their payments achieve. A trial would let the town examine whether protecting the meadow and keeping the bay useful can advance together.
q: How would the proposed equipment reduce damage?
choices: By keeping the connecting line off the bottom.
By moving young fish away from boat routes.
By letting roots hold heavier boat chains.
By spreading chains across wider areas.

subject: english
passage:
Volunteer handbook: A useful seed collection starts before anyone opens a storage jar. First, obtain permission and confirm the plant's identity with the botanical team. Check that its seeds are suitable for ordinary dry, frozen storage. Some kinds are damaged by drying or freezing and need different treatment. Taking an unfamiliar seed straight to a freezer may destroy the very thing you hope to protect.
During collection, take a small share of ripe seeds from many parent plants, leaving plenty for the wild population. This approach includes more of the natural differences within the population than taking a large quantity from a single plant. Keep collections from separate sites in separate bags. Attach the plant name, place, and date immediately. Without these records, living seeds may later be of limited use: workers may not know which local population a planting project would be restoring.
After delivery, staff clean and dry suitable seeds, then seal them against moisture before cold storage. A small sample is set aside for testing. Staff place these seeds under conditions that encourage growth and check how many sprout. Further samples are tested at intervals during storage. A jar full of seeds is not necessarily a jar full of future plants. Good records preserve the collection's identity; repeated growth tests tell us whether it still contains living material.
q: What is the handbook mainly intended to do?
choices: Compare the growth rates of wild plants.
Help visitors choose plants for home gardens.
Encourage volunteers to fill more storage jars.
Guide volunteers in making useful collections.
explain: 全文涵蓋採集前確認、採集方法、標示與保存檢測，目的在確保種子有保存價值。裝滿更多瓶子不等於留下可用的活種子。

April 9. The trail crew had removed the branches blocking the footpath but left the fallen trunk beside it. I thought they had stopped halfway through the job. The trunk looked untidy, and I asked a ranger why it remained. She suggested that I return after rain and look more closely. I noted the spot, though I expected to find little beyond wet wood.
June 2. Several seedlings were growing along the top of the trunk. Their thin stems stood above a soft green layer of moss. They had roots reaching into cracks rather than into the ground below. The ranger explained that the rotting wood held rainwater, giving these young trees a place to begin. I drew a line of seedlings in my notebook and wondered how long their wooden platform would last.
October 11. A piece of the trunk crumbled when the ranger gently pressed it. Beetles had made passages beneath the bark, and mushrooms appeared along one side. She described how insects and fungi break wood down, returning nutrients to the soil. The seedlings were still rooted on top, growing while their support gradually disappeared. On the way back, I noticed how neatly the open path ran past this busy patch of decay. My first entry had called the trunk unfinished work. I crossed out those words and added another date for a visit.
q: How are the three diary entries connected?
choices: Each walk tests a different way to remove wood.
Each date presents a different woodland guide.
Each visit adds evidence about the same object.
Each entry compares two separate forest trails.

subject: english

Interviewer: Your team raises freshwater mussels and releases them into rivers. Why do you hesitate to call release day a success? Coordinator: It is a beginning. Adult mussels filter tiny food particles from the water, and some can live for decades. A river could contain the same aging adults for years while its population quietly approaches an end. Raising and releasing more animals may hide that problem rather than solve it.
Interviewer: What might prevent a new generation? Coordinator: For many species, the young need a temporary fish host. At an early stage, they attach to the gills or fins of a suitable fish and continue developing there. Later they drop away and settle on the river bottom. Some mussels depend on particular fish species, so clear water alone does not guarantee that their life cycle can be completed. We assess both river conditions and the presence of suitable hosts before choosing a release site.
Interviewer: After a release, do you count young mussels too? Coordinator: Yes. Marks on the released animals help us keep their survival records separate from evidence of natural breeding. We also search for young that were born in the river, rather than supplied by our center. We want the population to take hold without repeated deliveries from us. That requires a place where a new generation can grow and eventually produce another.
q: Why does the interviewer end by asking about young mussels?
choices: To check whether marks on shells have faded.
To assess how quickly mussels grow in tanks.
To compare the diets of fish and adult mussels.
To separate lasting recovery from adult survival.
explain: 首段說長壽成蚌仍存活不代表族群延續，末段再追查河中出生的幼蚌，藉此區分存活與自然繁殖。問幼蚌不是為了測量養殖成長速度。

subject: english
passage:
A familiar flavor can hide an unfamiliar name. Vanilla, for instance, owes much of its commercial history to Edmond Albius, a boy born into slavery on Réunion, an island in the Indian Ocean. Growers had brought vanilla vines there from Mexico, but healthy leaves and beautiful flowers rarely led to the valuable pods. In Mexico, insects carried pollen between the flower's male and female parts. On Réunion, growers could not rely on this natural process.
In 1841, when Albius was twelve, he found a practical answer. A thin barrier inside the flower kept its male and female parts apart. Using a small stick, he lifted this layer and pressed the parts together, allowing pollen to reach the right place. The action took little time and required no costly equipment. Workers could learn the movement and repeat it flower by flower. A crop that had frustrated growers could now be produced on a much larger scale.
The result was a striking contrast. Vanilla helped create wealth, but Albius was not paid for his discovery. His freedom came in 1848 with the end of slavery in the French colonies, not as a reward for his skill. He later held poorly paid jobs and died in poverty. His life reminds us to ask who stands behind a successful product, and whether the people who create its value share in its rewards.
q: Which heading best captures the focus of this account?
choices: A Tropical Island and Its Changing Government
A Flavor That Required Expensive Equipment
The Young Discoverer Behind a Familiar Flavor
The Insects That Made Island Growers Wealthy
explain: 文章以 Albius 的授粉技術及其遭遇為主軸，適合以「熟悉風味背後的少年發現者」為題；昆蟲只是問題背景，並非使島上種植者致富的功臣。

On a walking path on La Gomera, one of Spain's Canary Islands, I heard a long whistle float across a steep valley. I looked up, expecting a bird. My guide smiled and answered with another whistle. A distant person then waved. What I had taken for a natural sound was part of a human exchange. The valley that separated the two speakers had become the space through which their message traveled.
The guide called it Silbo Gomero. It turns spoken Spanish into whistles by representing speech sounds through changes in pitch and breaks in the sound. These compressed signals carry language rather than a tune. Before phones, such messages helped islanders communicate across difficult ground without walking a long way. Hearing a whistle clearly, however, is different from understanding it. I could hear the distant speaker but could not make out the message; the guide could do both. A trained listener knows which patterns matter.
Later, passing a schoolyard, I heard pupils practicing. Lessons in Silbo Gomero have been part of education on the island since 1999. Their whistles made me rethink what I had heard on the path. A recording would preserve the sound, but these children were learning how to answer. I left with fewer photographs than expected and a stronger memory of listening: the island's past was reaching me through an activity that required someone else to respond.
q: Which statement best describes the narrator's changing understanding?
choices: A birdcall becomes a lesson in local wildlife.
A hike becomes a search for clearer phone signals.
An old performance inspires recordings of music.
A puzzling sound reveals a living local tradition.

A useful invention raises two different questions: does it work, and who developed it? Margaret Knight's paper bag machine had to survive both tests. Working in the American paper bag industry in the nineteenth century, Knight saw the value of bags with flat bottoms, which could hold purchases more conveniently than narrow, pointed bags. She developed a machine to cut, fold, and glue paper into that useful shape. The challenge was to coordinate several actions, not merely to draw a different outline on paper.
Knight built a wooden model and arranged for a metal version to be made. During this stage, Charles Annan saw the design and tried to claim it as his own invention. Knight challenged his claim. The dispute shifted attention from the machine's performance to the history of its development. A working model could demonstrate what the machine did, but its existence alone could not settle whose work had produced the design.
Knight could present drawings, notes, and witnesses who had seen her efforts at different stages. Together, these traced a process that had begun before Annan's claim. She obtained her patent in 1871. In this case, the records surrounding an invention mattered alongside the invention itself. The machine answered a practical need; the evidence helped establish her right to be recognized for answering it. Her success depended on being able to show both a result and the work that led to it.

choices: With praise for the choice of metal over wood.
With surprise at buyers' interest in flat bags.
With respect for her preparation and persistence.
With doubt about the evidence she had collected.

Does ketchup have to be red? The familiar bottle suggests an easy answer, but old recipes tell a more varied story. The name is connected to sauces made from salted fish in Asia. When British cooks adopted the idea, tomatoes were not the ingredient that defined it. For them, ketchup could be a concentrated sauce made from mushrooms or walnuts and added in small amounts to other food.
Did cooks in different places follow one fixed recipe? No. As the sauce moved between places, cooks drew on ingredients available to them. British versions and the recipes taken to North America were experiments rather than exact copies of one original mixture. Mushroom ketchup, for example, offered a strong savory taste without depending on fish. A shared name covered recipes whose contents and appearance could differ considerably.

So is a mushroom sauce falsely labeled ketchup? Historical usage suggests otherwise. Treating today's best-known recipe as the definition for every earlier one would erase the changes that produced it. The bottle on the table is a chapter in that history, not a description of the entire book.

From an old name to a proposed replacement.
From a familiar assumption to a broader view.

In a ceremony known as Shikinen Sengu, the main shrine buildings are rebuilt on neighboring sites every twenty years. The new structures follow the established form rather than introducing a fresh architectural fashion. A visitor searching for centuries-old timber may therefore misunderstand what has been preserved.
The practice keeps a different kind of record: knowledge held by people. Experienced carpenters work with younger ones, passing on ways of shaping and joining wood. Skills are handed down through real construction, with a completed building as the result. Repeated building provides occasions to practice those judgments and to correct mistakes under skilled guidance.

Ise simply asks us to consider another kind of continuity alongside the survival of physical objects. If we protect a building's appearance but lose the community able to produce it, something substantial has disappeared. When we call a building ancient, we often mean that its materials have lasted for centuries. That definition becomes harder to apply at Ise Jingu in Japan. In a ceremony known as Shikinen Sengu, the main shrine buildings are rebuilt on neighboring sites every twenty years. The new structures follow the established form rather than introducing a fresh architectural fashion. A visitor searching for centuries-old timber may therefore misunderstand what has been preserved.
The practice keeps a different kind of record: knowledge held by people. Experienced carpenters work with younger ones, passing on ways of shaping and joining wood. Skills are handed down through real construction, with a completed building as the result. A drawing can record dimensions, but it cannot give a beginner every judgment involved in working with a difficult piece of timber. Repeated building provides occasions to practice those judgments and to correct mistakes under skilled guidance.
This does not make old materials unimportant elsewhere. An ancient wall can carry evidence that no new wall could reproduce. Ise simply asks us to consider another kind of continuity alongside the survival of physical objects. If we protect a building's appearance but lose the community able to produce it, something substantial has disappeared. Preservation policy should therefore ask two questions: what should remain standing, and what should people continue learning to do? The age of the timber answers neither question by itself.

choices: It extends the shrine's method to other sites.
It ranks new copies above surviving structures.
It limits the scope of the shrine's example.
It shows why drawings lose their usefulness.

Dear Council Members, I run a grocery shop on Birch Street, where a line of parked cars occupies the curb from morning until night. Yet the street's needs change throughout the day. Shops receive boxes early, parents collect children in the afternoon, and restaurant customers arrive in the evening. Giving the same vehicles the same space all day does little to accommodate these different activities. I therefore support the proposed six-week trial of a curb with different uses at different hours.
Under the proposal, the space would be reserved for unloading in the morning, passenger pick-ups and drop-offs in the afternoon, and short visits in the evening. Some neighboring shopkeepers worry that a late delivery would have nowhere to stop. That concern deserves an answer: a nearby unloading space should remain available throughout the day. In addition, a clear strip leading to the shop doors must be kept free of boxes and vehicles, so people using wheelchairs will not have to take a detour.
Please judge the trial by more than the number of deliveries completed. Observers should also record whether customers can reach the doors easily and whether the backup unloading space is actually usable. A busy curb is not necessarily a successful curb. I would support changing the schedule if these observations reveal problems. The point of a trial is to learn how the street works, rather than to prove that the first plan was right.
q: What does the writer mainly seek to do?
choices: Request parking spaces for grocery shop owners.
Support a street trial with practical safeguards.
Report the results of a completed delivery trial.
Explain why evening unloading needs more space.
explain: 作者支持六週試行，並提出備用卸貨區及無障礙通道等配套。文章是在建議如何試行，並非報告已完成的結果。

subject: english
passage:
A screenshot announcing free entry to a neighborhood workshop spread through a local chat group. Several readers arrived expecting to use its tools without paying. At the door, they learned that only the guided tour was free. Angry messages soon followed, accusing the workshop of changing its offer after attracting visitors. The screenshot looked clear, and nobody had altered its words. What, then, had gone wrong?
A closer look at the full announcement supplied the missing explanation. The opening line offered free entry, but the next paragraph said that equipment use required a separate booking and fee. The person who shared the screenshot had cut off that paragraph to make the image fit a phone screen. The message retained its cheerful heading and the workshop's name, so it still looked complete. The problem was not a false sentence; it was a boundary that readers could no longer see.
This case shows why checking whether an image is genuine is only the beginning. Readers also need to ask what the message applies to and what may lie outside the frame. Opening the full notice would have answered both questions. Nor does the missing paragraph establish that the person who shared the image meant to deceive anyone. A desire to make a message convenient can remove the very detail that makes it accurate. Before passing on a clear-looking announcement, leave room for the information that gives it its limits.
q: Which title best fits this passage?
choices: Why Workshops Should Offer Free Equipment
How Chat Groups Attract Workshop Customers
When an Accurate Screenshot Leaves Things Out
Why Shorter Notices Make Workshop Rules Clearer
explain: 截圖文字未遭竄改，卻因缺少收費條件而誤導，這才是全文主旨。短訊息未必更清楚；被刪掉的限制正是誤會的原因。

Interviewer: Your furniture factory now uses an automatic fabric cutter. Has that made your work easier? Mara, senior operator: My shoulders say yes. I no longer move heavy cutting tools all day. But my attention has shifted. The machine follows a pattern beautifully until the material stretches or folds in an unexpected way. I spend more time examining fabric and deciding when the machine should stop.
Interviewer: Could a new employee simply learn the controls? Mara: The controls are easy; the judgment is harder. Yesterday, a sheet looked flat from above, but I felt a fold beneath it. Stopping the cutter saved the material. A new employee asked how I had noticed it. I could show her what to feel for, but a manual would struggle to capture every variation.
Interviewer: Do you have more time to teach now? Mara: On paper, yes. The cutting itself takes less time. In practice, the production target rose as soon as the machine arrived. I was expected to supervise more batches, so the minutes I had gained were quickly filled. Management has now reserved a weekly training period that cannot be used for extra production.
Interviewer: What would you tell another factory considering this machine? Mara: Plan for the work around it. Buying the cutter is one decision; deciding how people learn to use it well is another. If the experienced workers leave without passing on their judgment, the factory may own a fine machine and still waste a great deal of cloth.
q: What is the interview chiefly concerned with?
choices: How a factory selects patterns for its furniture
Why fabric cutting causes shoulder discomfort
How training manuals describe cutting controls
How automation changes the demands on workers
explain: 訪談由體力負擔減輕，談到判斷、產量與傳承需求，重點是自動化如何改變工作要求。肩膀負擔只是開頭的一項變化。
